page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it operates without a GPU.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier single-core execution in Geekbench (2258.0) and text processing (2843.0), alongside strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (35.11 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.8 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak, with stress-ng multi-core performance scoring 3485.37 and uncached memory read bandwidth limited to 32.39 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is average at 8.66 GB/sec, and LLM inference prompt processing for a 7B model reaches 33.72 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel computation or high memory write bandwidth. The presence of advanced CPU flags, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), provides hardware-level acceleration for cryptography and integer operations. This server is suited for single-threaded text processing, lightweight web serving, and memory-intensive applications with moderate CPU requirements, but it presents a tradeoff for highly parallelized database operations or compilation tasks.
